test_title: SSC GD Constable (2022) Official Paper (Held On : 23 Jan 2023 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: In a certain code language, ‘CHILL’ is written as ‘HDNHQ’ and ‘HARSH’ is written as ‘MWWOM’. How will ‘DEVIL’ be written in the same code language?
solution:
Here, we use the table given below:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/67823ce2220ce5cec6054744c5cd0cbdaee142cc2d29311ca69699a5c17da891.png] 

**Logic:** Addition of (5) and subtraction of (4) from the positional values of the alphabets alternatively.

‘CHILL’ is written as ‘HDNHQ’ →

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a13028deb182d36f52fe621b899708297f3c04b8df828d13edb13c6f2f197a00.png] 

'HARSH’ is written as ‘MWWOM’ →

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e82e4ace94f8642df91f1d7d2f308c032935322b424781e9e5cefb384b43ee55.png] 

Similarly, 'DEVIL' will be written as:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0fa1cc72e45c74dec45796728f691843c6e217b8279a79cd0dc8832dd6dde5da.png] 

Here, 'DEVIL' is written as** 'IAAEQ'.**

Hence, the correct answer is "Option (3)".
